american_english:
A Study of the Errors in Sentence Formation and Spelling of Students Studying in the Tibetan Refugee Camp Who Have Passed Class Five
Research procedure
The present research work has been prepared for the purpose of the Nepali Shikshan 598 course of the second year of M.Ed. under the Department of Nepali Language Education.
Objectives of the research: The present study is focused on such objectives as finding the errors that students studying in the Tibetan refugee camp who have passed class five make in the areas of sentence formation and spelling under standard Nepali, describing and analyzing those errors, finding the causes of those errors, and presenting suitable suggestions for eliminating those errors.
Outline of the research: The present research work has been classified into six chapters in total:
Chapter one: Under this chapter the title, purpose, statement of the problem, objectives, significance of the research and review of previous work are included.
Along with this, the sources of data collection, the method of data collection and the limitation of the study have also been placed.
Chapter two: In this chapter, information is given on the introduction of the Tibetan refugees, their way of living, their customs and, among the main problems they have faced in Nepal, the language-related problem.
Chapter three: In this chapter, an introduction to error analysis, the sources of errors, various kinds of errors and the process of error analysis are included.
Chapter four: In this chapter, the syntactic errors made by the refugee students are analyzed.
Chapter five: In this, an analysis is made of the errors of the refugee students in the aspects of spelling as well as word separation, word combination, punctuation marks, shirbindu and chandrabindu.
Chapter six: Under this chapter, a summary of chapters one through five, together with the causes of such errors and suitable kinds of suggestions for their elimination, are presented.
In addition to this, along with the need for further study, some possible titles for future study are also included.
Research method and procedure
For this research work, the collection of materials was made from Mount Kailash Residential School, Hemja-1, and S.O.S. Hermann Minor School, Chhorepatan, respectively, through the written and oral expression of 32/32 students who had passed class five.
Along with this, the present research appears to be focused on the use of classification and the analytical method.
Research findings
The main findings of this research are as follows—
• Among the refugee students, syntactic errors are seen at an average of only 64.64% in total.
• Of these, gender-related errors are seen at 89.61%, number-related errors at 79.69%, person-related errors at 95.31%, tense-related errors at 15.63%, aspect-related errors at 88.44% and honorific-related errors at 19.19%.
• In spelling errors, errors of omission and errors of addition are seen in particular.
• Similarly, errors are also seen in short and long vowels, word separation, word combination, shirbindu, chandrabindu and in the use of e, y, sh, ṣ and s.
• It is found that the students make errors because of such causes as not showing much interest in the Nepali subject, using English and Tibetan to a greater extent as the main medium of teaching and learning, and the ample influence of the mother tongue.
• Along with this, it appears that errors have occurred because the students did not exercise care in the organizational and spelling aspects as well while writing.

The present research work has been prepared for the purpose of the Nepali Shikshan 598 course of the second year of the M.Ed. programme within the Department of Nepali Language Education.
Objectives of the research: The present study is centred upon such objectives as discovering the errors which pupils studying in the Tibetan refugee camp who have passed class five commit in the fields of sentence construction and orthography in standard Nepali, describing and analysing those errors, discovering the causes of those errors, and putting forward suitable suggestions for the removal of those errors.
Outline of the research: The present research work has been divided into six chapters in all:
Chapter one: Within this chapter are comprised the title, purpose, statement of the problem, objectives, significance of the research and review of previous work.
In addition, the sources of data collection, the method of data collection and the limitation of the study have also been set down.

Chapter three: In this chapter, an introduction to error analysis, the sources of error, various types of errors and the process of error analysis are comprised.
Chapter four: In this chapter, the syntactic errors committed by the refugee pupils are analysed.

Chapter six: Within this chapter, a summary of chapters one to five, together with the causes of such errors and suitable kinds of suggestions for their removal, are presented.
Besides this, along with the necessity for further study, certain possible titles for future study are likewise included.

For this research work, material was collected from Mount Kailash Residential School, Hemja-1, and S.O.S. Hermann Minor School, Chhorepatan, respectively, from the written and oral expression of 32/32 pupils who had passed class five.
In addition, the present research would appear to be centred upon the use of classification and the analytical method.
Research findings
The principal findings of this research are as follows—
• Among the refugee pupils, syntactic errors are observed at an average of only 64.64% altogether.
• Of these, gender-related errors are observed at 89.61%, number-related errors at 79.69%, person-related errors at 95.31%, tense-related errors at 15.63%, aspect-related errors at 88.44% and honorific-related errors at 19.19%.
• Among orthographic errors, errors of omission and errors of addition are particularly observed.
• Likewise, errors are observed in short and long vowels, word separation, word conjunction, shirbindu, chandrabindu and in the use of e, y, sh, ṣ and s as well.
• It is found that the pupils commit errors owing to such causes as displaying little interest in the Nepali subject, making the greatest possible use of English and Tibetan as the principal medium of teaching and learning, and the abundant influence of the mother tongue.
• In addition, it appears that errors have arisen because the pupils did not exercise vigilance in the organisational and orthographic aspects either while writing.
australian_english:
A Study of the Errors in Sentence Building and Spelling of Students Studying at the Tibetan Refugee Camp Who Have Passed Class Five
Research procedure
This research paper was put together to meet the requirements of the Nepali Shikshan 598 course in the second year of the M.Ed. under the Department of Nepali Language Education.
What the research set out to do: The study homes in on finding the errors students at the Tibetan refugee camp who have passed class five make in sentence building and spelling in standard Nepali, sizing up and analysing those errors, tracking down what causes them, and putting up sensible suggestions for clearing them up.
How the research is laid out: The research paper has been split into six chapters all up:
Chapter one: This chapter takes in the title, purpose, statement of the problem, objectives, significance of the research and the review of earlier work.
As well as that, the sources for gathering facts, the method of gathering data and the limits of the study are set out too.
Chapter two: This chapter gives the lowdown on the Tibetan refugees, how they live, their customs, and, out of the main problems they have struck in Nepal, the language problem.
Chapter three: This chapter takes in an introduction to error analysis, where errors come from, the different sorts of errors and how error analysis works.
Chapter four: This chapter analyses the sentence-level errors the refugee students have made.
Chapter five: This one analyses the errors the refugee students make in spelling matters as well as in word separation, word joining, punctuation marks, shirbindu and chandrabindu.
Chapter six: This chapter puts up a summary of chapters one to five, along with the causes of those errors and sensible sorts of suggestions for clearing them up.
On top of that, along with the need for more study, a few possible titles for future study are thrown in as well.
Research method and procedure
For this research work, the material was gathered from Mount Kailash Residential School, Hemja-1, and S.O.S. Hermann Minor School, Chhorepatan, respectively, from what 32/32 students who had passed class five wrote and said.
As well as that, the present research comes across as focused on using classification and the analytical method.
Research findings
The main findings of this research come out like this—
• Among the refugee students, sentence-level errors turn up at an average of only 64.64% all up.
• Within that, gender-related errors turn up at 89.61%, number-related errors at 79.69%, person-related errors at 95.31%, tense-related errors at 15.63%, aspect-related errors at 88.44% and honorific-related errors at 19.19%.
• In spelling errors, errors of leaving things out and errors of adding things on turn up in particular.
• In the same way, errors also turn up in short and long vowels, word separation, word joining, shirbindu, chandrabindu and in the use of e, y, sh, ṣ and s.
• It turns out the students make errors because of things like not showing much interest in the Nepali subject, leaning heavily on English and Tibetan as the main medium of teaching and learning, and the strong pull of the mother tongue.
• Along with that, it looks like errors have come about because the students didn't keep an eye on the organisational and spelling side either when they were writing.

What the study was after: The present study is focused on things like finding out the mistakes that students staying in the Tibetan refugee camp who have passed class five make in sentence-making and spelling in standard Nepali, describing and analysing those mistakes, finding out why these mistakes happen, and giving suitable suggestions for clearing them.
How the paper is arranged: The present research work is divided into six chapters in all:
Chapter one: In this chapter the title, purpose, problem statement, objectives, importance of the research and review of earlier work are all included.
Along with that, the sources for collecting facts, the method of collecting data and the limits of the study are also put in.
Chapter two: In this chapter, information is given about the Tibetan refugees, how they live, their customs, and, out of the main problems they have faced in Nepal, the language problem.
Chapter three: In this chapter, an introduction to error analysis, where the errors come from, the different types of errors and the error analysis process are included.
Chapter four: In this chapter, the sentence-related mistakes made by the refugee students are analysed.
Chapter five: In this one, the mistakes the refugee students make in spelling matters as well as in word separation, word joining, punctuation marks, shirbindu and chandrabindu are analysed.

Besides this, along with the need for more study, a few possible titles for future study are also included.
Research method and procedure
For this research work, the material was collected from Mount Kailash Residential School, Hemja-1, and S.O.S. Hermann Minor School, Chhorepatan, respectively, from what 32/32 students who passed class five wrote and said.
Along with that, the present research seems to be focused on using classification and the analytical method.
What the study found
The main findings of this research are like this—
• Among the refugee students, sentence-related mistakes are seen at an average of only 64.64% in total.
• In that, gender-related mistakes are seen at 89.61%, number-related mistakes at 79.69%, person-related mistakes at 95.31%, tense-related mistakes at 15.63%, aspect-related mistakes at 88.44% and respect-related mistakes at 19.19%.
• In spelling mistakes, mistakes of leaving out and mistakes of adding extra are seen in particular.
• In the same way, mistakes are seen in short and long vowels, word separation, word joining, shirbindu, chandrabindu and also in the use of e, y, sh, ṣ and s.
• It is found that the students make mistakes because of reasons like not showing much interest in the Nepali subject, using English and Tibetan as much as possible as the main medium of teaching and learning, and the heavy influence of the mother tongue.
• Along with this, it looks like mistakes happened because the students did not take care in the organisational and spelling side also while writing.
